topline.text: ASCL (school/college leaders' union) has passed a motion of no confidence in Ofsted's leadership this week, citing unaddressed wellbeing harm from the report-card framework and threatening an industrial-action ballot.
NEU is pushing back on a ~£3.3bn teacher-pension contribution saving that DfE plans to claw back from school budgets from April 2027, rather than letting schools keep it.
2026 phonics check results are the first since the pandemic to match 2019 national levels (82% of Year 1) - but the disadvantage gap looks unmoved, flagged below as an uncertain figure.
Locally: South Yorkshire's Mayor has launched a Youth Impact Fund for 11-19 year-olds, and Sheffield councillors meet Monday to fund two secondary school expansions.

diary.text: Midday deadline for Sheffield secondary school applications for September 2027 entry (national deadline 31 Oct).
Sheffield Finance & Performance Committee votes on £602k funding for the Firth Park Academy expansion.
Extended deadline for schools to complete autumn census free school meals eligibility rechecks.

items.lede: ASCL declares no confidence in Ofsted leadership
items.body: The union's ruling council says it has seen no meaningful progress addressing wellbeing harm from the renewed report-card inspection framework, and wants inspections paused for an urgent review. Members will now be surveyed on a possible industrial-action ballot.

items.lede: NEU pushes back on £3.3bn pensions clawback
items.body: Employer pension contributions fall from 28.6% to 17.6% from April 2027, but DfE has confirmed school funding will be reduced to reflect the saving rather than schools keeping it, unlike a similar local-government pensions saving. NEU general secretary Daniel Kebede argues the money is urgently needed by schools.

items.lede: Phonics results back to pre-pandemic levels - gap claims conflict
items.body: DfE's 2026 phonics screening check shows 82% of Year 1 pupils met the expected standard, matching 2019 for the first time since the pandemic, with SEN attainment also at its highest since the check began. Commentators flag that more pupils not sitting the check flatters the headline, and reports disagree on whether the disadvantaged-pupil gap (cited variously at 4 or 17 percentage points) has actually narrowed - worth checking DfE's full release before quoting a figure.

items.lede: Mayor launches Youth Impact Fund for South Yorkshire's 11-19s
items.body: Oliver Coppard has launched grants of £2,000-£10,000 for talented young people aged 11-19 across South Yorkshire, covering coaching, equipment, course fees and travel - run with The King's Trust and South Yorkshire's Community Foundation, seeded with £25,000 from the combined authority. Teachers and community leaders can nominate pupils now.
items.action: Consider nominating MAPs pupils who'd benefit.

items.lede: Sheffield set to expand two secondaries for 2027-29 demand
items.body: The council's finance and performance committee meets Monday 19 October to approve passing £602,000 of government funding to Firth Park Academy (admission number rising 240 to 270) and a temporary 30-place expansion at Parkwood Academy, ahead of a projected secondary places deficit in 2027/28 and 2028/29.
